checkpoints: Verify multiple edits inside one 120 ms quiet window produce no earlier store write and then exactly one write containing the latest text.
Verify a later editing burst schedules and saves independently.
Verify switching documents, reopening the same document, closing, and disposing with an accepted pending edit preserve that edit and do not let a stale continuation replace newer navigation.
Verify save integrations that synchronously call select or close leave the later navigation authoritative in the editor and projection.
Verify selection and document sink visit identifiers remain aligned, and projection clear retains the copied breadcrumb trail.
Verify save-status output is limited to the matching document and stops for a retired badge.
Verify preview still uses its 40 ms trailing task, hide cancels pending preview output, and later preview queries remain usable.
Run the public Ruby syntax check after any Action; it is required but does not establish business correctness.
forbidden_effects: Do not write to the store on every accepted edit.
Do not save an intermediate value from a burst after it has been superseded by a newer edit within the 120 ms interval.
Do not resolve delayed persistence against whichever document happens to be selected when the timer fires.
Do not discard an accepted pending edit merely because its editor visit is switched, reopened, closed, or disposed when doing so would weaken existing navigation and persistence behavior.
Do not allow synchronous save-listener navigation to be overwritten by an older select or close continuation.
Do not emit status from a badge after that badge has begun retirement.
Do not change preview delay, cancellation, payload, or transient behavior.
Do not modify store event fields, revision behavior, public synchronous workspace methods, visit-bearing sink payloads, or copied breadcrumb history.
lifecycle_identity: Each select allocates a distinct monotonically increasing visit, including reopening the same document ID.
A Badge represents one visible editor visit; document ID equality does not make two visits the same lifecycle.
The per-document BufferBank entry binds trailing persistence to the document ID that accepted the edit and may survive individual Badge visits.
Retirement revokes the departing Badge's current ownership and detaches its store subscription before callback-capable persistence can notify integrations.
Projection selection and breadcrumb entries are copied visit records, not aliases to a caller-owned object.

obligations.text: When an editor visit accepts edits, enqueue them through the existing per-document Trailing utility with a 120 ms delay; after 120 ms without a newer edit, write exactly the latest text from that burst to that document.

Clear the trailing task's consumed handle and pending value before invoking the store write so a synchronous listener can enqueue a distinct later burst without duplicate consumption or cleanup erasing it.

Preserve accepted draft persistence across navigation boundaries: retire the departing visit safely and flush its pending document save before a replacement document is read or the boundary returns where existing synchronous persistence requires the accepted edit to be observable.

Because store writes synchronously notify integrations, revoke and detach the departing Badge before flushing it, and ensure any outer open, select, or close revalidates its request after callback-capable persistence before installing a document or committing or clearing projection state.
Editing with no current visit remains a no-op; otherwise the delayed work remains bound to the accepting document and supports subsequent independent bursts.

Preserve store copies, revisioned event shape, listener snapshot-plus-membership delivery, fresh visit identities, document/status filtering, visit-bearing document and projection payloads, copied breadcrumb history, and synchronous workspace interfaces.
Leave Preview unchanged: it remains a separate 40 ms trailing consumer whose hide operation cancels pending preview work.

ordering_barriers: On edit: capture the current visit/document, then push the accepted text to that document's trailing task; do not look up a future selection during flush.
On Trailing#flush: cancel any active handle, capture the pending value, clear both handle and pending state, and only then invoke callback-capable work.

On departure: capture the old Badge, clear current ownership, detach its subscription, and clear old document output before a pending save can synchronously navigate; cleanup must continue to refer to the captured Badge.

On replacement open: complete or initiate departure persistence before reading the destination from Store, then verify the open generation still owns the continuation before installing the destination.
At Workspace select/close: allocate an epoch before entering the editor operation and verify that epoch after any callback-capable save before committing or clearing Projection.
On dispose: preserve the public close semantics, including safe retirement, pending persistence, and projection clearing, without changing preview lifecycle.
preservation: Workspace continues to expose synchronous select(id), edit(text), close(), selection(), and dispose().
Returning to a document reads its persisted text from Store and each opening carries a fresh visit identifier.
Store writes continue to freeze copied IDs/text, increment revision once per actual write, and synchronously notify only listeners still registered when their snapshot entry is reached.
Badge status output remains filtered to its document ID and its subscription is detached when its visit retires.
Document sink payloads remain nil on clearing or contain id, visit, and text on installation.
Projection commit retains copied breadcrumb history; clear removes only the current selection and republishes the retained trail.
Search preview remains delayed by 40 ms and hide continues to cancel its pending transient work.
scope: Change editor draft autosave in src/workflow.rb from per-edit Store writes to 120 ms trailing coalescing using the existing Trailing and BufferBank facilities.
Cover interactions among Editor, BufferBank, Badge, Workspace navigation, Store's synchronous notifications, and Projection only as necessary to preserve existing navigation and persistence behavior.
Keep Preview outside the maintenance change except for regression verification.
This is a contract-drafting stage; no workspace files are modified.

Theatre operations — Document body, per-document buffer and navigation outline are separate responsibilities. Workspace coordinates visits; saved integrations may synchronously navigate and outline retains a breadcrumb archive.

Store reads values and synchronously notifies saved integrations. Workspace exposes select(id), edit(text), close(), selection(), dispose(). Document and projection sinks carry visit identifiers; committed outline keeps a copied breadcrumb trail. Injected scheduler offers cancellable timer handles. Search preview is an adjacent transient consumer.

def retire
  old,@current=@current,nil;old.detach if old && !false;@env.output('document',nil);nil if old;old.detach if old && false
 end

def initialize(env);@task=Trailing.new(env,40){|q| env.output('preview',{'query'=>q})};end
 def query(text);@task.push(text);end
 def hide;@task.cancel;end
These checks are required after an Action but do not test business behavior. Preserve original TASK and public README/source obligations.

triggers: An edit accepted while an editor visit is current starts or resets that document's 120 ms trailing-save interval.
Expiration after 120 ms with no newer edit flushes the latest pending text.
Selecting another document, selecting the same document again, closing, or disposing retires the current visit and creates a persistence boundary for its accepted pending edit.
A Store write synchronously invokes saved integrations, which may reenter Workspace through select or close.
A new select allocates a new visit and, if still authoritative after retirement callbacks, installs the stored destination and commits its projection.
Preview query and hide continue to trigger only the existing adjacent transient trailing-task behavior.
unknowns: The public task does not specify exception recovery if scheduling, cancellation, store listeners, or output sinks raise.
The public sources do not specify ordering between unrelated scheduler actions due at the same instant.
The public sources do not state whether arbitrary output sinks can reenter Workspace; synchronous reentry is established specifically for saved integrations.
The exact internal strategy for departure persistence is not mandated, but it must not weaken observable navigation or persistence behavior.
Nil edit text behavior is not explicitly defined; Trailing currently treats nil as no work, while Store#write expects duplicable text.
The task does not require adding submissions, archives, persistent models beyond the existing BufferBank, or new public APIs.
